item: a background job whose worker thread cannot start writes one warning of its own, for every caller
summary: BackgroundJob.start marked a job failed and re-raised when its worker thread could not be created, and 25 callers in other files neither answered nor logged it. It now writes one WARNING, 'background job <kind> did not start: <the job's own error text>' (the class and a fixed note, never the exception's words, since a start's arguments can hold a passphrase), after the job lock is released and under contextlib.suppress, and re-raises the original exception object with its chain. An interrupt and the already-running refusal log nothing. The three vLLM routes in llm.py lose their own line for the same refusal and keep their answers. Seven new tests in test_thread_start_interrupt.py plus the rewritten route test; 18 mutants killed. Limits: article_indexes.py:668, repair.py:759 and volume_job.py:173 still log a refused start themselves (other lanes' files), so those read twice; not observed in the field, driven by tests that inject the failure.
